knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Models and source

Xiao 2018 fitted the same inhibitory sigmoid Emax relationship between the
danofloxacin AUC24h/MIC index and the change in *Salmonella* Typhimurium load
separately in four matrices, and reports the four parameter sets side by side
in Table 2. They are packaged as four model files that share this vignette:

| Model file | Matrix | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `Xiao_2018_danofloxacin_rabbit_blood`  | Blood (log10 CFU/mL)  | Table 2, Blood column |
| `Xiao_2018_danofloxacin_rabbit_liver`  | Liver (log10 CFU/g)   | Table 2, Liver column |
| `Xiao_2018_danofloxacin_rabbit_spleen` | Spleen (log10 CFU/g)  | Table 2, Spleen column |
| `Xiao_2018_danofloxacin_rabbit_lung`   | Lung (log10 CFU/g)    | Table 2, Lung column |

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Xiao_2018_danofloxacin_rabbit_blood"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2018.00391> (PMCID: PMC5913287, open access)

None of the four models has a PK component. Xiao 2018 analysed serum
danofloxacin non-compartmentally (Table 1) and published no structural PK
model, so exposure enters through the covariate `AUC_DANOFLOXACIN_SERUM` (serum AUC0-24h
after one oral dose), which each model divides by its `mic` parameter to form
the AUC24h/MIC index.

```{r descriptions, results = "asis"}
organs <- c("blood", "liver", "spleen", "lung")
model_names <- paste0("Xiao_2018_danofloxacin_rabbit_", organs)
cat("**`", model_names[1], "`** -- ",
    rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(model_names[1]))$description, "\n\n", sep = "")
```

# Population

115 *S.* Typhimurium-free New Zealand rabbits aged 5-6 weeks and weighing
0.8-1.2 kg (sex not reported) were used at Yangzhou University, China. Systemic
infection was induced by two injections, 12 h apart, of 0.5 mL of a 10^8 CFU/mL
suspension of the virulent field strain HJ0310J into the ear marginal vein.
Twelve hours after the last inoculation the loads were 6.51 +/- 0.32 (blood),
6.56 +/- 0.26 (liver), 7.73 +/- 0.18 (spleen) and 7.32 +/- 0.32 (lung) log10
CFU/mL or CFU/g; the limit of detection was 2 x 10^3 CFU/mL or CFU/g.

* **Pharmacokinetics:** 30 infected rabbits, a single gavage dose of 1, 10 or
  30 mg/kg (n = 10 per dose), serum sampled at 0.25-24 h and analysed by
  HPLC-fluorescence (LOQ 0.02 ug/mL), non-compartmental analysis in WinNonlin
  6.1 (Table 1, Figure 3).
* **Efficacy:** 45 infected rabbits, 0.85% NaCl (control) or 1, 2.5, 5, 7.5,
  10, 15, 20 and 30 mg/kg by gavage once daily for 3 days from 12 h after
  infection (n = 5 per group); blood, liver, spleen and lung cultured 24 h
  after the last dose. These are the animals the four models were fitted to.
* **Susceptibility:** MIC 0.03 ug/mL and MBC 0.06 ug/mL in Mueller-Hinton
  broth, 0.06 and 0.12 ug/mL in rabbit serum; MPC 0.25 ug/mL. The broth MIC is
  the index denominator.

The same information is available programmatically:

```{r population}
p <- readModelDb("Xiao_2018_danofloxacin_rabbit_blood")()$population
str(p[c("species", "n_subjects", "age_range", "weight_range", "dose_range")],
    max.level = 1, width = 78)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` entry carries an in-file comment naming its source location. The
table collects them, plus the model equations, in one place.

| Equation / parameter | Value (blood / liver / spleen / lung) | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `Cc = e0 - imax * aucmic^hill / (ec50^hill + aucmic^hill)` | n/a | Materials and Methods, 'Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics Analysis' (printed with `+ Emax`); inhibitory sign settled by Figure 4 and the Table 2 '3 Log10 cfu/mL reduction' targets, see below |
| `aucmic = AUC_DANOFLOXACIN_SERUM / mic` | n/a | Materials and Methods, 'Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics Analysis' (AUC24h/MIC from the in vitro MIC and the PK) |
| `e0` (E0) | 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.01 log10 | Table 2, row E0 |
| `limax` (Emax) | 3.98 / 3.1 / 4.41 / 4.74 log10 | Table 2, row Emax |
| `lec50` (EC50) | 66.54 / 89.84 / 145.66 / 148.18 h | Table 2, row EC50 |
| `lhill` (N) | 1.86 / 2.47 / 1.90 / 1.26 | Table 2, row Slope (N) |
| `mic` | 0.03125 ug/mL (FIXED) | Results, 'In Vitro Pharmacodynamics': printed 0.03 ug/mL; the dilution step 0.03125 is the value the Results AUC24h/MIC column was divided by (Gate 2) |
| `addSd` | 0 (FIXED) | Not reported; the Results give only r^2 (0.8971 / 0.9186 / 0.9581 / 0.8708) |
| `AUC_DANOFLOXACIN_SERUM` | covariate | Table 1, row AUC24 h (1.55 / 11.70 / 28.10 ug*h/mL at 1 / 10 / 30 mg/kg); other doses by the linear regression stated in the Results |

# Gate 1 -- the inhibitory reading reproduces Table 2

The printed equation is `E = E0 + Emax * Ce^N / (EC50^N + Ce^N)` and Table 2
reports Emax as a positive number. Read literally, that makes E *increase* with
exposure. Figure 4, however, plots E falling from 0 towards -3 to -4 in every
organ, and Table 2 labels its last row the AUC24h/MIC 'for a 3 Log10 cfu/mL
reduction'. The fit is WinNonlin's inhibitory form, `E = E0 - Emax * ...`. The
Table 2 targets settle it: at each published target the inhibitory term must
equal 3.

```{r gate1}
tab2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~organ,   ~e0,  ~imax, ~ec50,  ~hill, ~target, ~r2,
  "blood",  0.00, 3.98,  66.54,  1.86,  121.30,  0.8971,
  "liver",  0.00, 3.1,   89.84,  2.47,  354.28,  0.9186,
  "spleen", 0.00, 4.41,  145.66, 1.90,  216.64,  0.9581,
  "lung",   0.01, 4.74,  148.18, 1.26,  228.66,  0.8708
)

# The transcription above must equal what the packaged models carry.
packaged <- bind_rows(lapply(organs, function(o) {
  ini <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(paste0("Xiao_2018_danofloxacin_rabbit_", o)))$iniDf
  v <- setNames(ini$est, ini$name)
  tibble(organ = o, e0 = v[["e0"]], imax = exp(v[["limax"]]),
         ec50 = exp(v[["lec50"]]), hill = exp(v[["lhill"]]), mic = v[["mic"]])
}))
stopifnot(
  isTRUE(all.equal(packaged$e0, tab2$e0)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(packaged$imax, tab2$imax)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(packaged$ec50, tab2$ec50)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(packaged$hill, tab2$hill)),
  all(packaged$mic == 0.03125)
)

gate1 <- tab2 |>
  mutate(term = imax * target^hill / (ec50^hill + target^hill),
         E_inhibitory = e0 - term,
         E_literal_plus = e0 + term)
gate1 |>
  select(organ, target, term, E_inhibitory, E_literal_plus) |>
  dplyr::rename("Organ" = organ, "Table 2 target AUC24h/MIC" = target,
                "Inhibitory term" = term, "E, inhibitory form" = E_inhibitory,
                "E, literal '+' form" = E_literal_plus) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

# GATE 1: the inhibitory term equals 3 at all four published targets. The
# parameters are printed to 3-4 significant figures, so the tolerance is 0.01.
stopifnot(all(abs(gate1$term - 3) < 0.01))
```

All four targets are reproduced to within 0.003 log10. For the lung, where
E0 = 0.01, the 3-log target is a 3.00 log10 reduction *from E0* (E = -2.99).

# Gate 2 -- the exposure regression and the MIC

The Results state that Cmax and AUC24h were linearly related to dose
(r^2 = 0.9592 and 0.9935) and that the AUC24h of the unsampled doses "could be
deduced according to a linear relationship". The regression coefficients are
not printed; refitting Table 1 recovers both r^2 exactly.

```{r gate2}
tab1 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~dose, ~cmax, ~tmax, ~thalf, ~auc24, ~clf, ~vzf,
  1,     0.18,  1.60,  15.30,  1.55,   0.45, 9.36,
  10,    1.80,  1.80,  14.01,  11.70,  0.76, 14.67,
  30,    3.49,  1.40,  11.38,  28.10,  0.84, 13.65
)
fit_auc  <- lm(auc24 ~ dose, data = tab1)
fit_cmax <- lm(cmax ~ dose, data = tab1)
coef(fit_auc)
c(r2_auc = summary(fit_auc)$r.squared, r2_cmax = summary(fit_cmax)$r.squared)

# GATE 2a: both r^2 match the paper at its printed four-decimal precision.
stopifnot(
  abs(summary(fit_auc)$r.squared - 0.9935) < 1e-4,
  abs(summary(fit_cmax)$r.squared - 0.9592) < 1e-4
)

results_index <- tibble::tribble(
  ~dose, ~aucmic_published,
  1,     76.42,
  2.5,   119.60,
  5,     191.56,
  7.5,   263.54,
  10,    335.50,
  15,    479.44,
  20,    623.38,
  30,    911.24
) |>
  mutate(auc_regression = predict(fit_auc, data.frame(dose = dose)),
         index_mic_003125 = auc_regression / 0.03125,
         index_mic_003 = auc_regression / 0.03)
results_index |>
  dplyr::rename("Dose (mg/kg)" = dose, "Published AUC24h/MIC" = aucmic_published,
                "Regression AUC24h (ug*h/mL)" = auc_regression,
                "Index, MIC 0.03125" = index_mic_003125,
                "Index, MIC 0.03" = index_mic_003) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

# GATE 2b: the published AUC24h/MIC column is the regression divided by
# 0.03125 ug/mL at every dose (rounding of the printed index, 0.05) ...
stopifnot(all(abs(results_index$index_mic_003125 - results_index$aucmic_published) < 0.05))
# ... and NOT the regression divided by the printed 0.03 ug/mL.
stopifnot(all(results_index$index_mic_003 - results_index$aucmic_published > 3))
```

The paper's index column is the regression divided by 0.03125 ug/mL, the
two-fold dilution step that the Results print rounded as 0.03. The packaged
`mic` is therefore 0.03125. Note that the published values at 1, 10 and 30
mg/kg are the *regression* values, not the measured AUC24h of Table 1 divided
by the MIC (49.6, 374.4 and 899.2); see the Errata for how Figure 4 plots them.

# Replicating Figure 4 -- the fitted sigmoids

```{r solve-helper}
# Solve one static exposure per row and key the result by an explicit index
# column, so comparisons join by value rather than trusting row order.
solve_static <- function(organ, auc) {
  mod <- readModelDb(paste0("Xiao_2018_danofloxacin_rabbit_", organ))
  ev <- data.frame(id = seq_along(auc), time = 72, evid = 0, amt = NA_real_,
                   AUC_DANOFLOXACIN_SERUM = auc, key = seq_along(auc))
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, keep = "key", returnType = "data.frame")
  stopifnot(nrow(out) == length(auc), !anyNA(out$Cc))
  out$Cc[order(out$key)]
}

sweep <- bind_rows(lapply(organs, function(o) {
  aucmic <- seq(0, if (o == "lung") 700 else 1000, by = 5)
  tibble(organ = o, aucmic = aucmic, E = solve_static(o, aucmic * 0.03125))
}))
```

```{r figure-4, fig.height = 6, fig.cap = "Replicates the fitted curves of Figure 4 of Xiao 2018. Dashed lines mark the 3 log10 reduction and the Table 2 targets; x-axis ranges follow the published panels."}
sweep$organ <- factor(sweep$organ, levels = organs)
targets <- tab2 |> mutate(organ = factor(organ, levels = organs))
ggplot(sweep, aes(aucmic, E)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -3, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_vline(data = targets, aes(xintercept = target), linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "grey50") +
  facet_wrap(~organ, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "AUC24h/MIC (h)", y = "E (change in log10 CFU/mL or CFU/g)") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r gate3}
# GATE 3: the right-hand ends of the fitted curves, digitised by the
# maintainers from the published Figure 4 raster by locating the curve's pixel
# row against the axis ticks: -3.96 (blood), -3.08 (liver) and -4.30 (spleen)
# at AUC24h/MIC of about 1000, and -4.14 (lung) at about 690. One pixel row is
# 0.02-0.04 log10 and the drawn line is 1-2 pixels thick, so the tolerance is
# 0.1 log10.
ends <- sweep |> group_by(organ) |> filter(aucmic == max(aucmic)) |> ungroup()
ends$digitised <- c(blood = -3.96, liver = -3.08, spleen = -4.30, lung = -4.14)[as.character(ends$organ)]
ends
stopifnot(all(abs(ends$E - ends$digitised) < 0.1))
# The control (index 0) returns E0 exactly.
stopifnot(all(abs(sweep$E[sweep$aucmic == 0] - tab2$e0) < 1e-12))
```

# Dose-response in each organ

The predicted change in load at each efficacy-study dose, with exposure from
the Results AUC24h/MIC column (control = 0).

```{r dose-response}
grid <- expand.grid(organ = organs, dose = c(0, results_index$dose),
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
  left_join(results_index |> select(dose, aucmic_published), by = "dose") |>
  mutate(aucmic_published = ifelse(dose == 0, 0, aucmic_published))
stopifnot(!anyNA(grid$aucmic_published))
grid$E <- NA_real_
for (o in organs) {
  i <- grid$organ == o
  grid$E[i] <- solve_static(o, grid$aucmic_published[i] * 0.03125)
}
grid |>
  select(organ, dose, E) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = organ, values_from = E) |>
  dplyr::rename("Dose (mg/kg/day)" = dose) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

```{r dose-gate}
# The predicted 3-log dose per organ from the inverted regression, for
# orientation (the paper does not compute doses: 'because of a lack of MIC
# data, we could not recommend the rational dose').
dose_for_target <- (tab2$target * 0.03125 - coef(fit_auc)[[1]]) / coef(fit_auc)[[2]]
setNames(round(dose_for_target, 2), tab2$organ)
# The liver needs the highest exposure, the blood the lowest, as the paper
# concludes from Table 2.
stopifnot(which.max(dose_for_target) == 2, which.min(dose_for_target) == 1)
```

# Why there is no PKNCA section

PKNCA validation does not apply. The four models are pharmacodynamic only: Xiao
2018 published non-compartmental PK (Table 1) and no structural PK model, so
there is no simulated concentration-time profile to integrate. The Table 1
exposures are used instead as *inputs*, and Gate 2 checks them: the
dose-exposure regression refitted from Table 1 reproduces both published r^2
values and all eight published AUC24h/MIC values.

A one-compartment model cannot be rebuilt from Table 1 either. With
first-order absorption the peak concentration can never exceed
`F * Dose / V`, yet the reported Cmax exceeds `Dose / (Vz/F)` at every dose:

```{r cmax-feasibility}
tab1 |>
  mutate(ceiling = dose / vzf, ratio = cmax / ceiling) |>
  select(dose, cmax, ceiling, ratio) |>
  dplyr::rename("Dose (mg/kg)" = dose, "Cmax (ug/mL)" = cmax,
                "Dose / (Vz/F) (ug/mL)" = ceiling, "Cmax / ceiling" = ratio) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
stopifnot(all(tab1$cmax > tab1$dose / tab1$vzf))
```

The profile is therefore at least biexponential, and no central volume,
absorption rate or intercompartmental clearance is reported.

# Assumptions, deviations and errata

**Adjudicated readings**

- **Sign of the effect.** The printed equation has `+ Emax` and Table 2 gives
  Emax as a positive number, which would make E rise with exposure. Figure 4
  and the '3 Log10 cfu/mL reduction' targets show a decline, and Gate 1
  reproduces all four targets with the inhibitory form `e0 - imax * ...`. The
  packaged models use that form, with `imax` = the Table 2 Emax. No value was
  changed.
- **The MIC is 0.03125 ug/mL, printed as 0.03.** Gate 2 shows the Results
  AUC24h/MIC column is the AUC regression divided by 0.03125 (within 0.03 at
  every dose), while dividing by 0.03 overshoots by 3.2-38. The broth MIC, not
  the twofold-higher serum MIC (0.06 ug/mL), is the denominator.

**Source inconsistencies (not resolved, no value adjusted)**

- **Figure 4 places three dose groups at measured, not regression, exposures.**
  Digitising the data columns of Figure 4 gives x-positions of about 50, 118,
  191, 264, 374, 479, 624 and 899 for the eight dose groups. Five match the
  Results column (119.60, 191.56, 263.54, 479.44, 623.38), but the 1, 10 and
  30 mg/kg groups sit at the *measured* Table 1 AUC24h divided by the MIC
  (49.6, 374.4, 899.2) rather than the listed 76.42, 335.50 and 911.24. Which x
  values the WinNonlin fit used cannot be decided from the paper; the
  packaged parameters are Table 2 verbatim either way, and a user can supply
  either exposure through `AUC_DANOFLOXACIN_SERUM`.
- **The lung fit has no 30 mg/kg group.** The published lung panel stops at
  AUC24h/MIC = 700 and its highest data column is at about 624 (20 mg/kg).
  The lung parameters should not be trusted beyond that exposure.
- **Blood reductions exceed the detection floor implied by the baseline.** The
  pre-treatment blood load reported for the infection model is 6.51 log10
  CFU/mL and the detection limit is 3.30 log10 CFU/mL (2 x 10^3), which caps a
  measurable reduction at about 3.2 log10. Figure 4 shows blood reductions
  down to about 4.3 log10 and a fitted Emax of 3.98. The efficacy-study
  baseline is not reported separately and the handling of counts below the
  detection limit is not described, so this cannot be reconciled from the
  paper.
- **Single-dose exposure, three-dose treatment.** The index uses the AUC24h
  after one dose, while the animals were dosed once daily for three days.
  With an 11-15 h terminal half-life the daily exposure rises over the course;
  the models carry the paper's single-dose definition.

**Not reported by the paper**

- **No residual error and no variability.** Only r^2 is given for each fit, so
  `addSd` is FIXED at 0 and no eta parameters are present. The models are for
  deterministic typical-value simulation and cannot produce a VPC.
- **No structural PK model and no time course of bacterial load.** The
  readout is a cross-sectional count per dose group 24 h after the last dose,
  so the models predict the change directly rather than integrating a
  bacterial density.
- **The in vitro time-kill curves (Figure 1) were fitted in GraphPad Prism,
  but no model form or parameters are reported,** so there is no time-kill
  model to package.
- No erratum or correction was found on Europe PMC (checked 2026-11-25).
